CodeMirror 5 — vendored source record
=====================================

WHAT IS HERE, AND WHY IT IS VENDORED
------------------------------------
Two editors use CodeMirror 5: the Settings page's Expert Mode (see
`services/webservice/static/settings-yaml.js` and
`services/webservice/templates/settings.html`) for YAML SYNTAX HIGHLIGHTING while the
operator types and the line-oriented marking of the lines a validation refusal names, and
the Site settings page's expert sheet (`services/webservice/static/site-config.js` and
`templates/site_config.html`) for the same two things over a CSS token sheet.

It is VENDORED ON PURPOSE — the console must work with NO NETWORK. No CDN is referenced
by any page or script; the files below are served from the shell's own `/static` area
(`/static/vendor/codemirror/...`), exactly like the language flags under
`services/webservice/static/flags/`. The flag SVGs set that precedent; this is its second
instance. A page that loaded the editor from a CDN would be a page the console cannot use
offline.

FILES
-----
  codemirror.min.js        CodeMirror 5 core                 (lib/codemirror.js)
  codemirror.min.css       CodeMirror 5 default stylesheet  (lib/codemirror.css)
  mode/yaml.min.js         the YAML mode                    (mode/yaml/yaml.js)
  mode/css/css.min.js      the CSS mode                     (mode/css/css.js)
  addon/hint/show-hint.js  the completion popup             (addon/hint/show-hint.min.js)
  addon/hint/show-hint.css the popup's own stylesheet       (addon/hint/show-hint.css)
  LICENSE                  the upstream MIT licence, verbatim

Every file comes from the SAME release as the core: a mode or an addon compiled against a different
minor version can call a helper the core no longer carries. An upgrade is therefore an ALL-OR-NOTHING
swap of the whole directory from one release.

The shell's own dark theme overrides the default stylesheet's colours (see the
`CodeMirror` rules at the foot of `services/webservice/static/shell.css`); the vendored
CSS is left BYTE-FOR-BYTE as upstream shipped it, so an upgrade is a plain file swap. The completion
popup's list, its rows and its selected row are restated from the shell's tokens the same way.

VERSION AND PROVENANCE
----------------------
  version:  5.65.16
  source:   https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/codemirror/5.65.16/codemirror.min.js
            https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/codemirror/5.65.16/codemirror.min.css
            https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/codemirror/5.65.16/mode/yaml/yaml.min.js
            https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/codemirror/5.65.16/mode/css/css.min.js
            https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/codemirror/5.65.16/addon/hint/show-hint.min.js
            https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/codemirror/5.65.16/addon/hint/show-hint.css
  licence:  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/codemirror/codemirror5/5.65.16/LICENSE

  mode/css/css.min.js sha256:         ee0ce00f346a6d7e345a74ab32f2cc600e8b7df878b28715d7d52192fa274eee
  addon/hint/show-hint.js sha256:     463814bdf21e4985890473c4424f69eb150e10d0817deb6e7cdad4ab379fd352
  addon/hint/show-hint.css sha256:    9058c1c14fcdae199b490bb6214f36a216b9ce84d7df2084830ebb6a60337651

`show-hint.js` is the MINIFIED addon served under the plain name the pages load; it is the upstream
file verbatim, as is the addon's stylesheet. Both are pinned by `tests/test_webui_configgen_hints.py`,
which re-hashes them against the sha256 above.

The CSS mode was checked against the same release's `mode/css/css.js` (npm
`codemirror@5.65.16`) by tokenizing the shipped brass sheet and a refusal line with both
files in a browser: the emitted token classes are identical. The classes it uses for this
project's content are `cm-variable-2` (a custom property's NAME — the mode treats `--x` as
a variable, not a declaration), `cm-property` (a declaration inside a rule), `cm-tag` and
`cm-variable-3` (a selector and its pseudo-class), `cm-callee` (a value's function name),
`cm-atom`, `cm-number`, `cm-string`, `cm-keyword` (`!important`), `cm-def` (an at-rule) and
`cm-comment`.
